bibliography.abstract: Dakar's residential rental market remains poorly documented despite its economic and social importance: 54.4% of households are renters, compared to 23.3% nationally. This study develops a complete machine learning pipeline to predict residential rents in Dakar, from data collection to model interpretation. An original dataset of 1,507 rental listings was built through systematic web scraping and a documented cleaning pipeline, then enriched with four purpose-built features, including a luxury score and a keyword-based quality score. Five models were compared: linear regression, Random Forest (baseline), XGBoost, and LightGBM optimized through Bayesian optimization with Optuna, using leakage-free KFold target encoding for location. The optimized XGBoost model achieved the best performance with an $R^2$ of 0.847, an MAE of 210,902 XOF, and an RMSE of 324,195 XOF. Feature importance was assessed using native XGBoost gain and SHAP values, revealing a substantial difference in the ranking of location, which appears as a minor predictor by gain but as the second most influential variable by SHAP. This result carries methodological implications for hedonic studies using target-encoded categorical variables. This study provides an interpretable benchmark for Dakar's rental market and highlights several avenues for improvement, including the integration of geospatial features and conformal prediction.
bibliography.title: Predicting Residential Rents in Dakar Using Machine Learning

en.caveats: The predictive models rely on a relatively small dataset of 1,507 scraped online listings, which may not fully represent the informal rental market in Dakar.
en.what: A machine learning pipeline was developed to predict residential rents in Dakar, Senegal, using a newly compiled dataset of 1,507 rental listings scraped from the web. The researchers engineered custom features, including a luxury score and a keyword-based quality score, and compared five models using target encoding for location. The optimized XGBoost model performed best, achieving an R² of 0.847, a Mean Absolute Error of 210,902 XOF, and a Root Mean Squared Error of 324,195 XOF.
en.why: It establishes an interpretable benchmark for a highly undocumented rental market where over half of the households rent, while demonstrating that SHAP values and native XGBoost gain yield highly divergent rankings for the importance of target-encoded location variables.
